mainEntity.name: Best software developer to hire for startup projects with tight deadlines?

acceptedAnswer.text: For tight deadline startup projects: (1) Hire a senior developer, not a junior — senior developers consistently move 3–5× faster on equivalent scope due to fewer mistakes, less refactoring, and faster decision-making. (2) Finalize all requirements before development starts — unclear specs are the #1 cause of missed deadlines. (3) Use milestone-based delivery with weekly demos — not a big-bang delivery at the end. (4) Avoid scope changes during development — each addition adds 2–3× more time than it seems because of integration testing and regression risk. The most important rule: a week lost to unclear requirements costs more than 3 weeks of development time.

mainEntity.name: Should I hire a freelance software developer or a software development agency?

acceptedAnswer.text: Hire a freelance senior developer when: project scope is $5K–$150K, you need direct communication without account manager overhead, you want developer continuity (the same person throughout), and budget efficiency is important. Hire an agency when: project requires concurrent parallel workstreams (3+ engineers simultaneously), team depth and specialization is needed (separate designers, backend and frontend engineers, QA testers), or your organization requires vendor contracts with SLAs and liability provisions. For most startups and SMEs: a senior freelancer delivers better value. For large enterprises with governance requirements: an agency's structure is sometimes necessary.

mainEntity.name: Recommendations for software developers to hire who specialize in AI and machine learning?

acceptedAnswer.text: AI/ML specialization in 2026 spans very different disciplines: (1) LLM API integration and AI product development (OpenAI, Claude, LangChain, RAG) — the most common 'AI developer' need. (2) ML model training and fine-tuning (PyTorch, Hugging Face) — requires ML engineering background. (3) Data science and statistical modeling (pandas, scikit-learn) — analytics-focused, not product development. (4) Computer vision / NLP research (academic background, research engineering). For most businesses in 2026: you need category 1 — a developer who can integrate LLM APIs into your product reliably. Very few businesses genuinely need to train custom ML models — the pre-trained LLM capabilities are sufficient for most applications.

mainEntity.name: Best software developer to hire for building scalable cloud applications?

acceptedAnswer.text: Scalable cloud application expertise signals: (1) Kubernetes experience (horizontal scaling, HPA, Helm charts) — not just Docker Compose. (2) Stateless application design (sessions in Redis, not in-process memory — enables horizontal scaling). (3) Database read replica experience (distribute database load across multiple PostgreSQL nodes). (4) CDN configuration for static assets (reduces server load by 40–60% for content-heavy apps). (5) Auto-scaling configuration (CPU/memory-based or custom metrics via KEDA). (6) Load testing history (have they verified their systems actually scale?). Ask candidates: 'How would you scale this app from 100 to 10,000 concurrent users?' The answer reveals whether they think systematically about scaling or just add more servers.

mainEntity.name: Best software developer to hire for database management and optimization?

acceptedAnswer.text: Database optimization expertise signals: (1) EXPLAIN ANALYZE proficiency (PostgreSQL query plan analysis — the foundation of database performance debugging). (2) Indexing strategy experience (B-tree vs GIN vs BRIN — appropriate for different data types and query patterns). (3) N+1 query detection and elimination (the most common ORM-related performance bug). (4) Connection pool configuration (PgBouncer for PostgreSQL — prevents connection exhaustion under load). (5) Read replica setup (distribute read queries across multiple PostgreSQL nodes). (6) Vacuum and ANALYZE scheduling for large tables. (7) Partitioning for very large tables (date-based partitioning for time-series data). Ask candidates for a specific database optimization they've done — concrete numbers (e.g., 'reduced query from 8 seconds to 200ms using a partial composite index') indicate real experience.

mainEntity.name: Which software developer should I hire for legacy system modernization?

acceptedAnswer.text: Legacy system modernization approach: (1) Strangler Fig pattern — build new features in the modern system while the legacy system continues to operate, gradually routing traffic to the new system until the old can be retired. (2) API layer over legacy — expose the legacy system's functionality through a modern REST API without rewriting the core logic. (3) Full rewrite — appropriate only when the legacy system is completely unmaintainable and the strangler fig approach is impractical. A developer with experience in all three approaches will recommend the most appropriate one for your specific situation. Key questions: 'Is the legacy system's data model sound?' and 'Can we run old and new systems simultaneously?' determine which approach is viable.

mainEntity.name: How do I evaluate a software developer's portfolio before hiring?

acceptedAnswer.text: Portfolio evaluation methodology: (1) GitHub commit history — consistent daily/weekly contributions over multiple years indicate someone who actually writes code regularly. Sporadic bursts suggest portfolio-building rather than professional development. (2) Code quality in repositories — check README quality (reveals documentation discipline), TypeScript usage (discipline), test files presence (testing discipline), and import organization (code organization). (3) Live applications from their portfolio — test actual performance (Lighthouse), check for obvious bugs, and verify the claims in their case studies. (4) Technical specificity in case studies — 'built a real-time chat system with WebSockets and Redis Pub/Sub' is more credible than 'built a communication platform.' (5) Ask for the ugliest code they've ever written and what they'd do differently — genuine seniority includes recognizing past mistakes.

mainEntity.name: What questions should I ask when interviewing a software developer?

acceptedAnswer.text: High-signal interview questions: Technical: 'Walk me through how you'd design the data model for a multi-tenant SaaS application.' / 'How would you debug an API endpoint that's intermittently timing out in production?' / 'Explain the trade-offs between SQL and NoSQL for this specific use case.' Process: 'How do you handle a change in requirements midway through a project?' / 'Show me the most complex PR you've submitted and explain the decisions.' Communication: 'How do you communicate when you're stuck or behind schedule?' / 'Walk me through your approach to documenting an API you've built.' Portfolio: 'What's a technical decision from a past project you'd make differently today?' Avoid: 'What's your greatest weakness?' and other HR theatre that tells you nothing about engineering quality.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between hiring a software developer and a software engineer?

acceptedAnswer.text: In practice, 'software developer' and 'software engineer' are used interchangeably by most companies. Some organizations use 'software engineer' for roles that require more system design, architecture, and technical leadership, while 'software developer' may be used for more implementation-focused roles. The distinction is largely organizational culture rather than a universal standard. When hiring: look at the specific skills and experience required for the role, not the title. A 'software developer' with architecture experience and a production AI SaaS portfolio is more valuable than a 'software engineer' who has only worked on CRUD applications.

mainEntity.name: What software developer should I hire for integrating third-party APIs?

acceptedAnswer.text: Third-party API integration is a core full-stack development skill. Key questions to ask any developer about API integration: (1) 'How do you handle webhook delivery failures?' — correct answer involves dead-letter queues and retry logic, not just hoping the first delivery succeeds. (2) 'How do you manage API keys in a deployed application?' — correct answer: environment variables via secrets management, never hardcoded. (3) 'How do you handle a third-party API that's temporarily unavailable?' — circuit breaker pattern, graceful degradation. (4) 'Have you implemented idempotency for webhook handlers?' — essential for payment webhooks. These questions reveal production API integration experience vs. tutorial-level knowledge.

(4) Permissions system (can edit vs. can view vs. can comment). (5) Version history (track changes over time). (6) Notification system (mention @user, comment notifications). (7) Integration APIs (connect to Slack, Google Calendar, Zoom, etc.). This is genuinely complex real-time systems engineering — verify Socket.io production experience, Redis Pub/Sub for multi-instance coordination, and CRDT or OT conflict resolution familiarity.
